sheet-118-1.description: The main map of sheet 118 covers the centre of the village of Hilton, today the eastern part of Maplewood Township in Essex County, at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Springfield Avenue, drawn 75 feet wide, crosses the top of the sheet with numbered frontages from 903 to 945. From its south side two 50 foot streets run down the sheet: Academy Street towards the south-east and Boyden Avenue from the right edge towards the south-west, meeting at the bottom of the sheet, with Burnet Avenue leaving Springfield Avenue at the left edge. The village is thinly built: frame dwellings and a few stores stand along Springfield Avenue, including a store holding the post office with scales in front of it, Pfau's Hotel on the north side, and the stables and wagon shed of the Hilton Hotel at the upper left, whose main building is drawn in the inset below. At the corner of Springfield and Boyden Avenues stands George Cope's carriage factory and blacksmith shop, a two storey frame building with the blacksmith shop below and a paint shop above. Between Academy Street and Boyden Avenue, on large lots, are the Hilton Public Library and School, a cruciform two storey frame building, and the M.E. Church, with a few dwellings. Most of the blocks numbered 1 to 4 are open lots with only scattered sheds and houses. Notes on the margins point to a frame barn 100 feet away and to the Union Chapel, 200 feet along Burnet Avenue, drawn in an inset on the right of the sheet. Two other insets on the lower half of the sheet show the Wheeler paste board mill at Waverly and the Maplewood grist mill.
notes: Academy (Academy Street) is today's Tuscan Road between Burnett Avenue and Boyden Avenue; it then left Springfield Avenue on its own, east of Burnet Avenue, where today it forks from Burnett Avenue 28 m south of Springfield Avenue.
Burnet Avenue is today's Burnett Avenue.
Hilton, Waverly and Maplewood appear only in the sheet title.
Buildings of note: Hilton Public Library and School, M.E. Church, Geo. Cope carriage manufactory and blacksmith shop, Pfau's Hotel, post office, Hilton Hotel stables.

Single sheet 118 of the Newark series, 50 ft to an inch (scale bar 7.54 px/ft). Five parts: 1 main map of Hilton (Springfield Av, Academy = today's Tuscan Road, Boyden Av, Burnet Av = Burnett Avenue), now east Maplewood; 2 inset of the Hilton Hotel on Springfield Av (overlaps the main map's upper left); 3 inset of Union Chapel on Burnet Av; 4 inset 'At Waverly, N.J.' (Wheeler Mfg Co paste board mill, a road, an alley and a P.R.R. side track); 5 inset of L. Pierson's Maplewood Mills (grist mill) on Valley St with mill pond and races.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Union Chapel on Burnet Avenue (no street junction; only Burnet Avenue drawn and its position along the street is given only as '200 ft' from a note on the main map; needs parcel corners matched to the chapel lot, or a historic map giving the chapel's position on Burnett Avenue).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: At Waverly, N.J., 1/4 mile east of the station: Wheeler Mfg Co paste board mill, an unnamed road, an alley and a P.R.R. side track (no named street or junction; Waverly (Newark / Hillside line) is outside the reference box and the road cannot be identified; needs identification of the mill site and road from another map, then a reference box over Waverly).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: L. Pierson's Maplewood Mills (grist mill), mill pond and races on Valley Street (only one street (Valley Street) drawn, no junction; needs the mill pond or a parcel corner identified on the ground (Pierson's Mill site on Valley Street, Maplewood)).

sheet-118-2.description: This inset at the left of sheet 118 redraws the Hilton Hotel on the north side of Springfield Avenue in the village of Hilton, today part of Maplewood Township, Essex County, because the main map cuts the hotel off at its left edge. It is drawn at the same scale of 50 feet to an inch and turned a few degrees against the main map, with its own north arrow. It shows the frontages numbered 901 to 907 on Springfield Avenue. The Hilton Hotel itself, a rambling two and a half storey frame building with several wings and porches, stands at the left by the frontage numbered 901 and 902. To its right is the hotel's yard with the Hotel Stables along the street front, a row of one storey frame stables, a long wagon shed behind them, a two storey stable building at the back and a smaller outbuilding. Small sheds stand along the lot line at the left, and a note at the top right gives the distance to a frame shed beyond. The lots further north are left blank. The stables and wagon shed are also drawn, less completely, at the upper left corner of the main map of the sheet, which this inset overlaps.
notes: Overlaps the upper left corner of the main map of the sheet, which draws the same stables and wagon shed; the two-storey stable building is drawn deeper here.
Placed from four building and lot corners carried from the main map (part 1), not from street junctions.
